# Odette Pullen

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c6 P4](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0004)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034)</sub>

## Appearance

Odette lost seven pounds in two weeks due to the stress of studying for exams at Regent's Academy.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P13](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0013)_

## Personality

Odette is unassuming, hardworking, dutiful, and steady, possessing a sensible nature and composure that contrast with her more imaginative and excitable friends. She lacks grand ambitions, remaining unbothered by high stakes as long as she meets her practical goals. Sensible and straightforward, she dislikes sentimentality or romance in her own writing because reading it aloud makes her feel foolish, though she appreciates material comforts like diamonds. Despite her composed exterior during exams, she is still prone to fretting or weeping heavily under severe emotional stress or relief.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047), [v1 c34 P21](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c35 P13](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0013), [v1 c36 P0](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0000)_

## History

Odette grew up in Brierley as the daughter of Gorham Pullen and Mrs. Alexander Tranter. While attending the local school under Mr. Pidgeon, she participated in childhood games, theatrical dialogues, and a girls' tale-writing club, while also nearly drowning during a boat outing on the Lake of Glassy Waters before her father saved her. She took part in playing the lily maid Elaine with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Opal Pettigrew, but panicked when Nell drifted out of sight on a flat boat. Upon entering the Regent's Entrance preparation class taught by Miss Thorne, she resolved to become a teacher to earn an independent living. She successfully passed the Entrance examinations and subsequently attended Regent's Academy, earning high marks in domestic science and passing her final tests with steady composure. Following her qualification, she accepted a position from the Stonebridge trustees to teach at their school.
